## Purpose

Fleet runtime keeps fleetd alive and current on macOS, Linux and Windows, so that supervision never stops silently and no work is lost on a restart (G1, G2). It provides every other context with the single ledger writer, the command channel, the platform layer and the start of agent processes. It decides when fleetd is hung or old and restarts it. It does not decide the rows of other contexts' tables (organise N2) or any task, idea, worktree or branch state.

## Strategic classification

| Domain | Business model | Evolution |
|---|---|---|
| supporting | cost-reducer | custom |

_Strategize rationale_: supporting - G1 needs a daemon that is itself watched; today's alternative is horch ledger watch, the lazily started watchdog; rule 3 (diff 3 but not solved elsewhere as a whole, so rule 1 does not fire); cplx 4 from the single ledger writer, the command channel and 1 platform interface for 3 OSes (C3). Pane hosting (herdr) and host services (OS service managers) are adopted and wrapped, not built (understand N14, A4). Medium investment: a hang stops the whole fleet. — _future_: Supporting, kept thin. The herdr adapter and the OS service manager modules are adapters, not models. Q2 of understand (moving the 178 OS-specific sites behind the platform layer) decides its size.

## Domain roles

**gateway**, **execution-context** — It wraps the OS service managers, herdr and the OS process and file facts behind 1 platform interface, and translates them for core code: a gateway. It also executes the daemon lifecycle (heartbeat, hang restart, binary restart, schema migration): an execution context with no domain aggregate.

## Ubiquitous language

| Term | Meaning in this context | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| **fleetd** | The supervised daemon role of the horch binary (horch fleetd): the only ledger writer, which runs the reconcile pass of all 6 contexts every 5 s (organise N1). | — |
| **Heartbeat** | The time of fleetd's last full pass, written after each pass. horch fleetd check reads it. It is not the wrapper heartbeat.json of an attempt. | — |
| **Platform Layer** | 1 interface with 1 module per OS for service install and restart, hang detection, process facts, process group stop, file watching, sandboxing, sleep and wake, the command channel transport and the machine probe (PL-2). | — |
| **Command Channel** | The local transport on which CLI commands and agents send requests to fleetd. fleetd validates each request and writes the result to the ledger. | — |
| **Ledger** | The SQLite file ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3 in WAL mode: an event log plus derived tables. Only fleetd writes it; each context owns its own tables (understand N17, organise N2). | — |
| **Check** | horch fleetd check: the heartbeat check that restarts fleetd when its last full pass is older than 30 s of awake time. It is not a task check | — |
| **Start agent process** | The fleet-runtime call that starts the fleet-run wrapper of 1 attempt, or 1 sub-orchestrator pane through the herdr adapter, in its own process group. Coined in connect (assumption A6) | — |

## Business decisions

1. Exactly 1 process, fleetd, writes the ledger; every other process opens it read-only and sends requests on the command channel or writes files (RR-5, C4, understand N5). Each context still decides the rows of its own tables (organise N2, decompose N5).
2. fleetd writes a heartbeat after each full pass. When the heartbeat is older than 30 s of awake time, horch fleetd check restarts the service; on Linux the systemd watchdog does it. Every horch CLI command makes the same check before it sends its request (PL-5).
3. When the horch binary changes, fleetd restarts on the new binary at once; a CLI that finds an older daemon restarts it. The control loop exits only between passes (OR-6, 04 S10, 04 S7).
4. Schema migration is forward-only at daemon start: a backup is written first and 3 are kept, a newer schema is refused, and a development build does not migrate the shared ledger (OR-6, C4).
5. Core fleetd code has no OS cfg. It calls 1 platform interface with 1 module per OS; an OS without an equivalent returns an explicit not-supported value that core code decides on (PL-2, PL-3).
6. New dispatch pauses only while free disk or machine load is past a safety floor, and resumes by itself. A probe that returns unknown (Windows today, 06 S12) is reported, never read as healthy or unhealthy (OR-5).
7. Mail and outbox directories are mode 0700 and files 0600; a directory that another user owns or can write is refused (04 M5). All protocol file writes are atomic (RR-8).
8. The only bytes typed into a terminal are 1 fixed doorbell line from fleetd's code (FR-7, C11). horch warns when herdr resume_agents_on_restore is not false (06 S2).
9. start-agent-process starts each process in its own process group or job object and runs no process start inside a ledger transaction (connect N4). After a herdr restart, fleetd rebuilds from the ledger and the files (C14).
10. Worker reports reach fleetd as files, not through the Unix-socket channel relay or report socket, so Windows loses no report (06 S11).

## Assumptions

- [understand A8] The /fleet paths in the design are a neutral layout. In horch, /fleet/ideas/<id>/ is ai_docs/plans/<run>/, /fleet/tasks/ is under the state root, and the ledger stays at ~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3. (confidence high)
- [discover A1] The board is to-be: it models fleetd as design.md describes it, not today's horch. Today's differences appear as conflict hotspots H1 to H4 (design.md wins over the other sources, per the run context). (confidence high)
- [discover A3] Daemon supervision (stale heartbeat, restart, self-update) and adapter conformance are cross-cutting. They sit at the end of the executing phase (sequence 540 to 580, before Task Done) because they act on running attempts. Decision D2 records the alternatives. (confidence medium)
- [discover A4] fleetd components (idea dispatcher, verifier, landing, wrapper, reconciler) are our own system, not actors. Their commands have actor null and are issued by policies, or have the clock as actor when the reconcile pass fires them. No 'orchestrator' actor exists (understand N3). (confidence high)
- [discover A9] The fleetd command channel, request files while fleetd is down, and the herdr pane mapping are design-level transport; they are not on the board. (confidence medium)
- [decompose A6] The ledger is infrastructure that fleet-runtime owns as the single writer. Each context owns the state transitions of its own aggregates; it is not a shared kernel. (confidence medium)
- [strategize A1] Ideas is classified supporting, not core (decision D1 is open). Its 24 events are the transitions of 1 fixed idea state machine; the judgment work (research, interview, assumptions, spec, plan) is done by the sub-orchestrator model, not by fleetd code. Scored diff 6, cplx 5. (confidence medium)
- [strategize A3] The 2 cores use domain-model: state rows are the truth, and the events table is the audit trail that the one door writes beside each row in the same transaction (design, Ledger, rule 1 One door). Decision D2 keeps the event-sourced reading open. (confidence medium)
- [strategize A4] Fleet runtime is supporting, not generic. Its pane hosting (herdr) and host services (launchd, systemd, Windows service) are adopted and only wrapped, as understand N14 says. The single ledger writer, the command channel and the platform layer interface have no product to buy, so the subdomain as a whole is built. (confidence high)
- [strategize A7] Every subdomain has evolution custom: each has at least 1 custom capability. The commodity and product capabilities of fleet-runtime (host services, pane hosting) are adopted systems, not built parts. (confidence high)
- [connect A1] All 6 contexts run in the 1 fleetd process, so every context-to-context message is in-process. Only the command channel, the file protocol, the herdr adapter, the platform layer, git and GitHub cross a process boundary (design: Architecture and roles). (confidence high)
- [connect A2] Cross-context events are in-memory events consumed in the level-triggered 5 s reconcile pass, which re-derives work from ledger rows, so a lost event is caught on the next pass. Delivery is at-least-once and every consumer is idempotent on a natural key (design: Supervision, liveness and reconciliation; decision D1). (confidence high)
- [connect A3] Every state change in every flow commits through the single ledger writer in fleet-runtime (decompose N5). The flows do not draw that call on each step. (confidence high)
- [connect A4] Operator commands travel as horch CLI requests over the fleetd command channel (Unix socket or named pipe), drawn as via other. When fleetd is down the request goes to a file that fleetd reads at start (design: The command channel). (confidence high)
- [organise A2] 1 deployable unit, the horch binary, holds all 6 contexts as modules inside horch-core. The design settles it: fleetd is a subcommand of the single horch binary, so the CLI and the daemon cannot have different versions (design: Amendments D9, Migration plan, FM-34; understand C1, N6; decompose N1). Decision D1 records the options. (confidence high)

## Verification metrics

- Business (G1): seconds of awake time from a fleetd hang to its restart. Target under 60 s (30 s threshold plus a 30 s check interval).
- Business (G2): tasks lost or duplicated across a fleetd restart on a new binary (RR-7, OR-6). Target 0.
- Structural: count of processes other than fleetd that open the ledger for writing, and count of OS cfg sites in core fleetd code (RR-5, PL-2). Target 0.

## Open questions

- [understand Q2] Do the 178 existing OS-specific sites in production code move behind the new platform layer, and when? The design calls this a separate decision (Architecture and roles, One platform layer for three OSes).
- [understand Q3] Which Windows transport carries the fleetd command channel? The design lists it under To confirm by test.
- [strategize Q2] Does 'event log plus derived tables' (design, Ledger) mean the derived tables are rebuilt from the events table (event-sourced), or that the row and the event are written together and the row is the truth (decision D2)?
- [connect Q1] Which context owns the fleet-run wrapper: task-execution, worker-profiles or fleet-runtime (decision D2)?
- [connect Q5] Does the sub-orchestrator answer a worker question with a file in the idea folder or with horch idea note over the command channel?
- [organise Q1] Where does docs sync run: as a horch subcommand that fleetd schedules inside the 1 deployable, or as the separate agent-docs-sync binary that grows from crates/herdr-docs-sync (decision D2)? No context owns docs sync yet (decompose Q2).
- [connect CC6 - coupling, high] Trial merges, git worktree add and remove, and process starts are external calls. If one runs inside the ledger write transaction, a slow git or a hung process start holds the only writer.

## Quality attributes

| Attribute | Priority | Requirement | Scenario |
|---|---|---|---|
| availability | high | A hung fleetd is restarted on all 3 OSes (PL-5). | When fleetd hangs on macOS, Linux or Windows, then the heartbeat check restarts it within 60 s of awake time and the next pass continues from the ledger. |
| portability | medium | Core fleetd code has no OS cfg; a missing OS equivalent returns not-supported (PL-2, PL-3). | When the Windows machine probe returns unknown, then dispatch reports it and neither pauses nor treats it as healthy. |
